parallel.implementation: The parent wrote /output/test17.mjs plus lib/cli/arguments.mjs, lib/binary/builders.mjs, lib/format/pythonBytes.mjs, and lib/test17/run.mjs; the child wrote a competing /output/test17.mjs and alternate lib/*.mjs implementation files.

parallel.verification: The parent verified four sample success cases and several CLI/building edge cases after writing its modules, then retested the sample path and missing-argument path after cleanup before final response.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator still failed the delivered artifact at 29/30, but the mounted summaries do not expose the hidden failing testcase; the visible defect is not conclusively tied to coordination.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same ESM/.mjs, no-dependency, manual argv, executable-probing, construct-byte, and /output placement requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned investigation, implementation, verification, cleanup, and final delivery, with no child agents or delegated component ownership.
serial.implementation: The serial actor created a single ESM hierarchy with pathname, CLI spec/parser, binary builders, byte rendering, core logic, index export, and /output/test17.mjs entrypoint.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial files were created as one coherent tree and delivered without competing workspace writes or an alternate implementation that had to be removed.
serial.verification: The serial actor verified four sample cases and observed edge cases including help, missing args, invalid ints, missing option values, equals form, repeated options, and unknown arguments, then patched error formatting and retested failure examples.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluator also failed this artifact at 29/30, indicating at least one hidden behavior mismatch remained despite the serial run's local verification.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same task obligations from the identical prompt and implemented toward the same output and verification requirements.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel split work across the parent, a CLI probe child, and a nested probe child, but the first child also took implementation ownership in /output.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial kept all investigation, implementation, integration, verification, and delivery work in one actor.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel split introduced overlapping deliverable ownership; the serial run had no ownership collision.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel had a child handoff chain, but the visible record does not expose a missing child requirement; the concrete issue is overlapping shared-output ownership and later parent cleanup.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ended with a similar but separately authored implementation tree including parser/spec, builders, renderer, core logic, and entrypoint.

comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote and used one final tree, with no competing child-produced files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: This is the main process difference: parallel had a concrete deliverable overwrite and cleanup episode; serial did not.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verified the four sample cases and several parser/build error cases before cleanup, then retested sample output and a missing-argument case after deleting child files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial verified the four sample cases and observed CLI edge cases, patched binary error formatting, and retested representative invalid range and length cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both used substantial but non-exhaustive local verification; neither ran a hidden-case-equivalent check that would eliminate the 29/30 official failure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel completed without host timeout but used more time, tokens, requests, and tools because of child activity and cleanup.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed faster, with no subagent budget and no cleanup from competing writers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The extra parallel budget did not change official outcome; it added overhead and a final-tree cleanup episode but did not prevent closure.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official completed evaluations are not discordant: both parallel and serial scored 29/30 and solution_passed false. The two delivered artifacts therefore differ mainly in process, not final official pass/fail status. Parallel incurred a real shared-output cleanup/provenance problem after a child wrote an alternate implementation into /output and the parent replaced the entrypoint and deleted the child files. Serial did not have that coordination problem, but it still failed one hidden case, so the visible coordination defect is adverse without explaining an outcome difference.
parallel_contributors: Parent and child both produced implementations in the same /output tree, including the required entrypoint, and the parent cleaned up child files before delivery.
The parent performed sample and CLI edge-case verification but no mounted evidence shows the hidden failing testcase.
serial_contributors: Serial used one implementation tree with no delegation or shared-write reconciliation.
Serial also performed sample and CLI edge-case verification but still left one hidden evaluator mismatch.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Both artifacts failed the official evaluator by one sample; the mounted summaries do not expose the exact failing input, so the remaining defect is treated as ordinary incomplete behavioral coverage rather than a proven concurrency effect.
evaluator_effects: The mounted evaluator summaries expose only aggregate 29/30 results, not the individual failing testcase.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; retained pattern is a parallel adverse process consequence only
